A Gaussian-plume concentration field on a grid

Source: R/plots.R
plmfld.Rd

Evaluates gplume at every point of an x by y ground-level grid (or at height z) and returns the field as a matrix with the axes, ready for plot(). Use it to map where the plume from a single stack touches the ground, how far downwind the highest concentration lies, and how wide the affected area is.

Usage

plmfld(q, u, h, x, y, z = 0, stab = "D", set = "rural", mixh = NULL, nimg = 3)

Arguments

q, u, h, stab, set, mixh, nimg

As in gplume: emission rate (mass per second), wind speed (m/s), effective stack height (m), Pasquill class "A" to "F" (default "D"), "rural" (default) or "urban", mixing-lid height in metres (default NULL, no lid), number of lid image pairs (default 3).

x, y

Numeric vectors, strictly increasing: the downwind and crosswind coordinates of the grid, in metres from the source.

z

Numeric scalar, the receptor height in metres; default 0 (ground level).

Value

A list of class rmbl_field: field (a numeric matrix of concentrations, rows along x, columns along y), x, y, dx and dy (median spacings, NA for a single coordinate), units ("concentration") and title (character, used by the plot method).

Details

Every grid point \((x_i, y_j, z)\) is passed to gplume in one call, with the source at the origin and the wind along \(+x\); the field is therefore zero (or vanishingly small) upwind and at \(x \le 0\). The concentration is in the mass unit of q per cubic metre (grams per cubic metre for q in grams per second). dx and dy are the median grid spacings, used by the plot method for the cell size. The cost is one plume evaluation per grid point, so a 100 by 100 grid is 10,000 evaluations.

Errors: x or y not numeric or not strictly increasing; z negative; and every check of gplume (q, u, h, the stability class, the setting, the mixing height).

See also

gplume; plot() draws the field as an image with contours (see plot-methods).

Examples

f <- plmfld(
  100,
  5,
  50,
  x = seq(100, 3000, by = 100),
  y = seq(-500, 500, by = 50)
)
dim(f$field)
#> [1] 30 21
plot(f)


# where the ground-level maximum lies, downwind
f$x[which.max(apply(f$field, 1, max))]
#> [1] 800

# a more unstable atmosphere brings the plume down sooner
fb <- plmfld(
  100,
  5,
  50,
  x = seq(100, 3000, by = 100),
  y = seq(-500, 500, by = 50),
  stab = "B"
)
fb$x[which.max(apply(fb$field, 1, max))]
#> [1] 300

# the coordinates must increase
try(plmfld(100, 5, 50, x = c(300, 100), y = c(-50, 0, 50)))
#> Error : `x` and `y` must be strictly increasing receptor coordinates
